entities.name: PMID:25070523
observations: In male C57BL/6 mice aged 4 or 18 months, 5 weeks of Lieber–DeCarli ethanol diet reduced global bulk-liver 5hmC in young mice but not old mice; the age-by-alcohol interaction was significant (p=0.009).
Young ethanol-fed mice had hepatic 5hmC of 0.22 ± 0.01% versus 0.29 ± 0.06% in young controls (p=0.004); old controls had 0.24 ± 0.02% versus 0.29 ± 0.06% in young controls (p=0.04).

entities.name: PMID:25574465
observations: An age-only C57BL/6 mouse liver study reported higher global hepatic 5hmC in old than young males: 0.32 ± 0.02% versus 0.24 ± 0.01% (p=0.02).

entities.name: PMID:32221779
observations: A mouse liver study spanning 4–32 months reported a significant global decline in 5hmC with age; it did not test alcohol or an age-by-alcohol interaction.

entities.name: PMID:38482502
observations: A 2024 alcoholic-fatty-liver study implicated TET2 deficiency in alcoholic fatty liver disease and Srebp1 regulation, but the reported abstract did not test aging, global hepatic 5hmC, or an age-by-alcohol interaction.

entities.name: Age-alcohol-5hmC interaction
observations: In bulk liver DNA from male C57BL/6 mice, ethanol lowered global 5hmC in young but not old mice; the formal age-by-alcohol interaction was significant (p=0.009).

entities.name: Age-related TET decline
observations: In the direct interaction study, hepatic Tet2 and Tet3 mRNA were lower in old than young mice (p<0.005); a significant age-by-alcohol interaction for transcripts was not reported.
